scheme_name: Financial Assistance to Non Governmental Organisations
description:
The Financial Assistance to Non-Governmental Organisations scheme was launched by the Ministry of Women and Child Development in India in 2009. 

This scheme aims to provide financial support to NGOs that are working towards the welfare of women and children. 

The primary objective of this scheme is to empower women and children through various initiatives and programs. 

It also seeks to enhance the capacity of NGOs to deliver services effectively. 

The government allocates a specific budget each year for this purpose. 

For the financial year 2022-2023, the budget allocation for this scheme was approximately INR 100 crores. 

This funding is intended to support projects that focus on issues such as health, education, and social welfare. 

The scheme is designed to promote gender equality and improve the socio-economic status of women and children. 

Eligible NGOs can receive financial assistance for a variety of activities. 

These activities include awareness campaigns, skill development programs, and educational initiatives. 

The financial assistance provided under this scheme can range from INR 5 lakhs to INR 50 lakhs per project. 

The exact amount of funding depends on the nature and scope of the project proposed by the NGO. 

To be eligible for this financial assistance, NGOs must meet certain criteria. 

The organization must be registered under the Societies Registration Act of 1860 or the Indian Trusts Act of 1882. 

It should have been operational for at least three years prior to applying for assistance. 

The NGO must have a proven track record of working in the field of women and child welfare. 

Additionally, the organization should have a clear and transparent financial record. 

The application process for this scheme involves several steps. 

First, the NGO must submit a detailed project proposal to the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

This proposal should outline the objectives, methodology, and expected outcomes of the project. 

It must also include a budget breakdown detailing how the funds will be utilized. 

The proposal should be accompanied by the NGO's registration certificate and audited financial statements for the last three years. 

Once the proposal is submitted, it undergoes a thorough evaluation process. 

The Ministry reviews the proposal based on its relevance, feasibility, and potential impact. 

If approved, the NGO will receive a sanction order detailing the amount of financial assistance granted. 

The disbursement of funds is typically made in installments based on the progress of the project. 

The first installment is usually released after the signing of a Memorandum of Understanding. 

Subsequent installments are released upon submission of progress reports and utilization certificates. 

The timeline for the application process can vary. 

Generally, NGOs are encouraged to submit their proposals by the end of the financial year. 

The Ministry usually announces the results of the evaluation within three to six months of the application deadline. 

The implementing authority for this scheme is the Ministry of Women and Child Development. 

The ministry has a dedicated team that oversees the evaluation and disbursement of funds. 

Contact details for the Ministry can be found on their official website. 

They provide a helpline for NGOs seeking assistance with the application process. 

In addition to financial assistance, the scheme also offers capacity-building support. 

This includes training workshops and seminars aimed at enhancing the skills of NGO staff. 

The government also encourages collaboration between NGOs and local government bodies. 

This is to ensure that the projects align with the overall development goals of the region. 

Statistics indicate that over 1,000 NGOs have benefited from this scheme since its inception. 

The scheme has successfully funded projects that have reached millions of women and children across India. 

In 2021 alone, approximately 150 projects were sanctioned under this scheme. 

These projects focused on various issues such as nutrition, education, and health care. 

The impact of these projects has been significant in improving the quality of life for many beneficiaries. 

The scheme also promotes innovative solutions to address the challenges faced by women and children. 

NGOs are encouraged to propose unique and effective strategies in their project proposals. 

The government regularly reviews and updates the guidelines for this scheme. 

This is to ensure that it remains relevant and effective in addressing the needs of the target population. 

The Ministry also conducts field visits to assess the implementation of funded projects. 

Feedback from these visits is used to improve future funding strategies. 

Overall, the Financial Assistance to Non-Governmental Organisations scheme plays a crucial role in supporting civil society efforts. 

It empowers NGOs to implement impactful projects that contribute to the welfare of women and children in India. 

The scheme has become an essential part of the government's strategy to promote social development. 

It reflects the commitment of the Indian government to enhance the role of NGOs in societal progress. 

By providing financial assistance, the government aims to create a more equitable society. 

This scheme is a vital resource for NGOs striving to make a difference in their communities. 

The continued support from the government is essential for the sustainability of these initiatives. 

As of October 2023, the scheme remains active and continues to accept applications from eligible NGOs. 

The government encourages more organizations to participate in this initiative. 

This is to maximize the impact of welfare programs aimed at women and children across the nation.
